evaluated.name: This screen (Storescope)
strengths: Sees the exact banner, toast, and button the merchant is looking at.
Can draw an arrow on the control to click next.
Works from a tab share or an OS screenshot — no store credentials.
weaknesses: OCR can miss tiny validation text or low-contrast toasts.
Cannot click Shopify for you or see pages that are not on screen.
evaluated.use_when: A red/yellow banner, toast, or validation state is visible right now.

evaluated.name: Shopify Community & Reddit
strengths: Real merchant wording: “payouts on hold”, “test mode still on”, “no shipping methods”.
Often includes the exact banner screenshot and what finally cleared it.
Good for rare Risk/Trust holds that docs under-describe.
weaknesses: Staff replies cannot see your account and default to “contact support”.
Advice goes stale after admin IA changes.
Threads mix owner-only steps with staff-permission dead ends.
evaluated.use_when: The banner is vague (“standard review”) and you need the usual next email/team.

evaluated.name: Official Shopify Help
strengths: Canonical click paths (Settings → Payments → Manage).
Correct distinction: PayPal is not a primary card provider.
Safe default when the banner names a documented feature.
weaknesses: Account-hold pages stay high-level on purpose.
evaluated.use_when: You already know the feature name and need the official steps.

evaluated.name: Shopify Sidekick
strengths: Lives in admin and can read store data (orders, products, some settings).
Can draft changes with an approve-before-save gate.
Fast for “how is my store doing” and form-filling.
weaknesses: Trained for prose and docs — merchants report hallucinations on exact codes, recent features, and theme/app placement.
Cannot see a screenshot of a toast that already dismissed.
Does not confirm whether an app embed is actually live on the published theme.
Owner-only Risk tickets still bounce to email.
evaluated.use_when: You want Shopify to act on store data after Storescope names the exact screen.

evaluated.name: Perplexity
strengths: Cites current help pages and forum threads.
Useful to check whether a banner text is a known 2026 issue.
weaknesses: No access to your admin or this capture.
Citations can still be wrong or mixed across plans/countries.
evaluated.use_when: You want a sourced second opinion after the local playbook match.

evaluated.name: ChatGPT
strengths: Good at turning a pasted banner into a checklist.
Strong when you paste the OCR text Storescope already extracted.
weaknesses: No live admin, no arrow, often outdated menu names.
Will invent Settings paths that do not exist on your plan.
evaluated.use_when: You need a longer written plan *after* the screen is identified.

evaluated.name: Gemini
strengths: Strong at reading a screenshot you upload.
Useful multimodal backup if OCR in-browser is weak.
weaknesses: Uploading an admin screenshot leaves your browser — customer names, payouts, keys.
Still generic on Risk holds and country-specific Payments.
evaluated.use_when: You have already paused/redacted the capture and need a visual second pass.

evaluated.name: Grok
strengths: Picks up very recent social complaints (X) about outages or holds.
weaknesses: Noisy, not store-specific, weak on official click paths.
evaluated.use_when: You suspect a platform-wide outage, then verify on status.shopify.com.

evaluated.name: Kimi
strengths: Long-context reading of pasted help docs or a long thread.
weaknesses: Same blind spot as every generic model: it cannot see this admin tab.
evaluated.use_when: You drop a long official doc or forum thread next to the OCR text.

recommendation: Identify the banner locally first. Hand Sidekick a pre-filled prompt only after the playbook names the cause. Use forums/Perplexity for rare holds. Do not upload raw admin screenshots to a cloud model unless you have paused and redacted.
